Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

satisfy verb

a need, hunger or desire

also satisfy one’s hunger, quench one’s thirst, satisfy a craving, satisfying

classical

Cic. Sen. 26 (Lewis & Short): quasi diūturnam sitim explēre cupiēns
Phaedr. 4.18.5: famem (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 374

expleō, explēre, explēvī, explētum

verb, second conjugation, transitive

satisfy, fill up (hunger, thirst, a desire)

Literally “fill full”; so to satisfy a need as if filling it with food: famem, sitim, cupiditātem, dēsīderium explēre (Lewis & Short). It also means to complete a number or a time, and to make good a loss.

Other words

  • satiō, satiāre, satiāvī, satiātum — satisfy fully, sate, fill

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.25 (Lewis & Short): dēsīderia nātūrae; Ov. M. 11.371: famem (Lewis & Short)

    To give enough or more than enough, so often “glut”, of hunger, anger or hatred. Not to be confused with satiō, satiōnis, a sowing.

Examples

  • dēscende, amīce; tanta bonitās est aquae, voluptās ut satiārī nōn possit mea

    come down, friend; the water is so good that I can’t get enough of itPhaedr. 4.9.3–9

  • quās (litterās Graecās) sīc avidē arripuī quasi diūturnam sitim explēre cupiēns

    which (Greek literature) I seized as greedily as if I wanted to quench a long thirstCic. Sen. 26 (Lewis & Short)

See also satisfy, be hungry, enough, desire.
